intended_object: The canonical isomorphism, in any category C, between the pushout of a span f : X ⟶ Z, g : X ⟶ Y in C and the unop of the pullback of f.op and g.op in Cᵒᵖ. This is the duality between pushouts in C and pullbacks in Cᵒᵖ. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition is faithful. It builds the iso as the unique-up-to-iso comparison of two colimit cocones on the same span:
- the chosen pushout colimit, and
- the unop of the chosen limit cone on `cospan f.op g.op`, which `PullbackCone.isLimitEquivIsColimitUnop` turns into a colimit cocone.

The needed `HasPullback f.op g.op` instance is supplied by the instance just above the definition (lines 326–327). The lemmas that follow (`pushoutIsoUnopPullback_inl_hom` and `_inr_hom`) show that the iso is the canonical one: it carries `pushout.inl` and `pushout.inr` to the unops of the pullback projections. It is stated for an arbitrary category with only the existence of the pushout assumed, which is the natural generality. It is the dual companion of `pullbackIsoOpPushout`, so it is not too narrow.
